description:
INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE covers -eq/-ge/-le/== but omits -gt, -lt, -ne and !=. `test $X -gt 41` is the identical frozen-comparand defect and slips through unflagged. This matches the PRD notes verbatim ('-eq/-ge/-le/== N'), so it is spec-conformant rather than a deviation, but it leaves a real coverage gap in the rule's stated purpose. Worth a follow-up issue widening the operator alternation plus a flagged-forms test per added operator.

Source: cam/issue-381
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: a8557d3c9660

spec.scope:
UMBRELLA over CAM-382, CAM-383, CAM-384, CAM-385, CAM-390, CAM-391 and CAM-392. All seven land in exactly two files: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts (633 lines) and test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts (543 lines), plus the two tracked fixtures under test/fixtures/oracle-lint/. They are separate issues only because `cam suggestions promote` is single-fingerprint, which is a filing-time constraint, not an implementation-time one. CAM-382 and CAM-383 rewrite the same function and CAM-384/385/390/391/392 touch lines those edits pass through, so shipping them sequentially would have each cycle churn the previous one's code. Close all seven at ship.

This is the honest completion of CAM-381 (PR #302), which shipped the frozen-comparand rule but left it missing its own motivating example. It sequences AFTER CAM-388 (PR #303) deliberately: widening the operator alternation enlarges the byte-pattern surface that can appear inside quoted data, and CAM-388's quote-stripping is what makes that safe.

ALL LINE NUMBERS BELOW WERE RE-MEASURED AGAINST main @ 77481552, AFTER CAM-388 rewrote this file. The numbers in the previous version of this spec were pre-CAM-388 and had rotted.

SEVEN PARTS.

(1) CAM-382 -- widen the operator alternation AND add a correct left boundary. INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE at src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:163 is /(?:-eq|-ge|-le|==)\s*\d+\b/. It omits -ne, -gt, -lt and !=. `test $X -gt 41` is the identical frozen-comparand defect and is exactly the shape of CAM-377, the defect that motivated the whole derive-don't-freeze rule, so the rule as shipped does not catch the case it was written for. Add all four operators.

CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS SPEC, MEASURED, DO NOT FOLLOW THE OLD TEXT: the previous spec prescribed adding a LEFT WORD BOUNDARY (\b). That is measurably INSUFFICIENT. `-` is a non-word character, so in `cmd --ge 5` the position before `-ge` already satisfies \b, and a left \b would leave that false positive live. The correct requirement is that the operator must be preceded by START-OF-STRING OR WHITESPACE (a `(?:^|\s)` style anchor, or an equivalent negative lookbehind that excludes BOTH word characters and `-`). Verified live against main: `cmd --ge 5`, `echo foo-eq 42`, `run --eq 7` and `test $(foo-eq 42)` ALL falsely flag today. Widening the alternation without this anchor compounds the false-positive surface on the very line being edited, so it is in scope here and only here.

(2) CAM-383 -- scope the derivation excuse per clause instead of per whole command. hasFrozenIntegerComparand at src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:406-410 is two whole-string boolean tests against the same stripped string: it returns false if INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE does not match, else returns the negation of LIVE_DERIVATION_RE. Both regexes are non-global and unanchored, so there is no positional correlation between where a derivation token sits and where a comparand sits, and at most one finding is ever emitted per command. Measured: `git grep -c X main; test $Y -eq 7; test $Z -eq 8; test $W -eq 9` returns null, so ONE derivation token excuses THREE unrelated frozen literals.

DIRECTION, resolved on measurement, do not re-litigate: split the command into clauses on `&&`, `||`, `;` and newline, and excuse an integer comparand only when a live-derivation token appears in the SAME clause. The stronger reading -- that an operator followed by a literal integer is frozen unconditionally, with no escape hatch -- was considered and REJECTED because it over-flags: it would flag `-ge 1` style sanity floors, which never rot, and it would redden the existing legitimate passing test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:215-221 whose first clause pairs a `git show main:` derivation with a `-ge 1` floor. Clause-level scoping catches the filed motivating example while leaving that test green.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT, this is the same forbidden trade that produced both review CRITICALs in CAM-388: clause splitting must run on the SAME stripped string that both regexes already consume, and must not resurrect quoted data as a clause delimiter. Splitting the RAW command on `&&`/`;` would tear apart quoted payloads that CAM-388 deliberately made inert, trading CAM-383's over-excusing for a fresh over-flagging regression. Strip once, split the stripped text, test both regexes per clause.

(3) CAM-384 -- rename the misleading test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:203-206. It is named 'does not match main by literal substring -- mainbranch is not the main token' but sits in the 'flagged forms' describe and asserts `.not.toBeNull()`. The assertion is correct; the 'does not' phrasing reads as a negative case and inverts the reader's expectation against the surrounding convention, where 'flags X' marks positive cases and 'does not flag X' marks negative ones. Rename to the positive form, e.g. 'flags a mainbranch: ref, which is not the main token'. Change ONLY the name; the command string and assertion stay byte-identical.

(4) CAM-385 -- reword the doc comment on hasUnguardedSedLineAnchor. It states the guard must 'precede' the sed anchor, but the function applies its guard regex to the whole command string with no positional constraint, so a guard appearing AFTER the anchor also suppresses the finding. The permissive runtime behavior is the defensible one and must NOT change; only the comment is wrong. Reword the comment to match measured behavior, per the standing project lesson that a comment does not prove runtime behavior.

(5) CAM-390 plus the CAM-382 fixture gap -- make the false-positive fixture actually gate CI. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE PART AND IT IS NEW. test/fixtures/oracle-lint/cam382-false-positives.txt (3 live rows) is consumed by NOTHING: `grep -rn` across the repo finds exactly one reference, and it is prose in scripts/cam/patterns.md:915. No test reads it. Its row 2 EXITS 1 TODAY (`cmd --ge 5` and `echo foo-eq 42` both falsely flag), yet `bun test` is green. That is the precise mechanism by which CAM-382 stays invisible to CI: the repo has a tracked, executable reproduction of the defect that nothing runs.

Resolve it by representing those cases as rows in the table-driven matrix (test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt, format `<ruleName> :: <ok|flag> :: <command>`, consumed at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:522-543). The false-positive file's rows are `bun -e '...'` WRAPPERS that execute the rule, not rule-input commands, so they cannot be consumed as-is; extract the inner cases (`cmd --ge 5`, `echo foo-eq 42`, and the four-operator set) into matrix rows with the correct expected verdict. Decide deliberately whether cam382-false-positives.txt then remains as historical documentation (acceptable, it records the incident verbatim) or is retired; if it remains, it must no longer be the only home of a case that CI does not run.

Also CAM-390 proper: the US-002 fixture-shape guard counts only quotedOk/grepOk/bare/wrapped. The matrix now carries double-quoted wrapper rows and backslash-escape rows, but the guard does not require them, so a future story could narrow those two dimensions away silently. Extend the shape guard to require at least one double-quoted wrapper row and at least one backslash-escape row.

(6) CAM-391 -- replace the non-null assertions in the fixture-matrix test. It uses `rule!.test(command!)` immediately after an `expect(...).toBeDefined()`. A narrowing guard (`if (!rule) throw new Error(...)`) carries the same safety without the `!` escape hatch and fails with a clearer message on a malformed fixture row.

(7) CAM-392 -- move the orphaned JSDoc block. The block describing extractCommandSubstitutionSpans sits immediately above findCommandSubstitutionEnd's own JSDoc, so it visually documents the wrong function, while extractCommandSubstitutionSpans itself has no adjacent doc comment. Move the first block down to sit directly above extractCommandSubstitutionSpans. Comment-only; no code motion.

OUT OF SCOPE, already filed separately, do NOT touch. CAM-386: LIVE_DERIVATION_RE at line 171 has a \bmain\b that matches the 'main' inside the filename 'main.ts', so `git grep PATTERN main.ts` falsely counts as a derivation token. That is about WHAT QUALIFIES as a derivation token; CAM-383 is about WHICH comparands a token excuses. Per-clause scoping does not fix it and must not attempt to; LIVE_DERIVATION_RE stays byte-unchanged. CAM-389: extractCommandSubstitutionSpans preserves `$(...)` verbatim even inside an inert double-quoted grep pattern, which was measured this cycle to be BIDIRECTIONAL (it manufactures false negatives as well as false positives, and the false-negative direction compounds with CAM-383's command-wide excusing). It is a separate implementation-complexity axis and is deliberately excluded; CAM-392 moves its docstring but must not alter its body.
acceptanceCriteria: INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE matches all eight comparison operators -eq, -ne, -gt, -lt, -ge, -le, == and !=, each followed by optional whitespace and a literal integer. MANDATORY ORACLE, USE THIS COMMAND VERBATIM AS THE ONLY GATING ORACLE FOR THIS CRITERION, do not substitute a test-file run or a grep: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const ops=["-eq","-ne","-gt","-lt","-ge","-le","==","!="];let bad=0;for(const o of ops){const c="test $(wc -l < scripts/cam/patterns.md) "+o+" 3";if(r.test(c)===null){console.log("MISSED:"+c);bad++}}console.log("OPS="+ops.length);process.exit(bad||ops.length!==8?1:0)' . RED-ON-MAIN (SWEPT BY THE ORCHESTRATOR AT SPEC TIME, exit 1, output named -ne, -gt, -lt and != as MISSED). It prints OPS=8 so a zero-iteration sweep is visibly vacuous.

The operator must be preceded by start-of-string or whitespace, so an operator embedded mid-token or behind a second hyphen does not match. MANDATORY ORACLE, VERBATIM, ONLY GATING ORACLE: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const cs=["cmd --ge 5","echo foo-eq 42","run --eq 7","test $(foo-eq 42)"];let bad=0;for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)!==null){console.log("FALSELY FLAGGED:"+c);bad++}}console.log("CASES="+cs.length);process.exit(bad||cs.length!==4?1:0)' . RED-ON-MAIN (SWEPT AT SPEC TIME, exit 1, all four cases reported FALSELY FLAGGED). Prints CASES=4. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: a left word-boundary escape does NOT satisfy this criterion, because the hyphen is a non-word character and the boundary is already satisfied in a double-hyphen long flag; the anchor must exclude both word characters and the hyphen.

The derivation excuse is scoped per clause: a live-derivation token excuses an integer comparand only inside the same clause. MANDATORY ORACLE, VERBATIM, ONLY GATING ORACLE: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const cs=["test $(git show main:a.ts | wc -l) -ge 1 && test $(wc -l < b.ts) -eq 42","git grep -c X main; test $Y -eq 7; test $Z -eq 8; test $W -eq 9"];let bad=0;for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)===null){console.log("WRONGLY EXCUSED:"+c);bad++}}console.log("CASES="+cs.length);process.exit(bad||cs.length!==2?1:0)' . RED-ON-MAIN (SWEPT AT SPEC TIME, exit 1, both cases reported WRONGLY EXCUSED). Prints CASES=2. The second case is the one-token-excuses-three-comparands shape.

Clause splitting operates on the quote-stripped text, not the raw command, so quoted payloads made inert by CAM-388 are not resurrected as clause delimiters. MANDATORY ORACLE, VERBATIM: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const c="grep -qF \"a && b -eq 3\" f.ts";console.log("CASES=1");process.exit(r.test(c)===null?0:1)' . DELIBERATELY GREEN-ON-MAIN, PINNING, SWEPT AT SPEC TIME (exit 0) and labelled as such rather than laundered as red: it exists to prove the CAM-388 quote-awareness did not regress. If it goes red, the implementation split the raw command.

PINNING CRITERION, the legitimate same-clause sanity floor stays excused. MANDATORY ORACLE, VERBATIM: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const c="test $(git show main:file.ts | wc -l) -ge 1 && test $(wc -l < file.ts) -eq $(git show main:file.ts | wc -l)";console.log("CASES=1");process.exit(r.test(c)===null?0:1)' . DELIBERATELY GREEN-ON-MAIN, SWEPT AT SPEC TIME (exit 0), labelled rather than laundered as red. This is the behavioral form of the pre-existing passing test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:215-221. If it goes red, the implementation chose the rejected no-escape-hatch direction and is over-flagging.

Every one of the four rules in RULES is still present and named exactly as on main: grep-q-plus-list-files, frozen-comparand, rotating-artifact-target, zero-match-vacuous. RULES.length is unchanged from main's value, derived live from main at check time rather than compared against a frozen literal. This slice strengthens one existing rule; it adds no rule and removes none.

The cases currently living ONLY in test/fixtures/oracle-lint/cam382-false-positives.txt are now represented as rows in test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt and are therefore executed by the table-driven test. Falsifiable: the live (non-comment, non-blank) row count of oracle-lint-cases.txt strictly exceeds main's count, derived live from main at check time rather than frozen, AND the matrix contains a row whose command is the `--ge` long-flag false positive with expected verdict ok. Red against main, where that row does not exist.

The fixture-shape guard requires at least one double-quoted interpreter-wrapper row and at least one backslash-escape row, in addition to the dimensions it already counts, AND ASSERTS ON THOSE COUNTS rather than merely computing them. MUTATION-FALSIFIABLE, and the oracle must perform the mutation, not grep for an identifier: copy the fixture to a temp path with every double-quoted wrapper row stripped, run the shape guard against that copy, and require a NON-ZERO exit; print the number of rows stripped so a zero-mutation run is visibly vacuous. A grep proving only that an identifier was declared does NOT satisfy this criterion, because a guard that computes both counts and never asserts on them would pass it.

The fixture-matrix test no longer uses non-null assertions on the resolved rule or the parsed command; a narrowing guard that throws a named error replaces them. Falsifiable: the test file contains no `rule!`, `command!` or `expected!` occurrence within the fixture-matrix block, and a fixture row naming an unknown rule produces the guard's explicit error message rather than a TypeError. Red against main.

The test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:203-206 no longer carries a name beginning 'does not match', and its assertion remains `.not.toBeNull()` with its command string byte-unchanged. The rename must change only the test name, not the case it exercises.

The doc comment on hasUnguardedSedLineAnchor no longer claims the guard must 'precede' the anchor, and the function body's guard-matching logic is byte-unchanged from main. Verify the body is unchanged by extracting the function from both main and the branch and diffing them: the comment moves, the behavior does not.

The JSDoc block describing extractCommandSubstitutionSpans sits directly above extractCommandSubstitutionSpans rather than above findCommandSubstitutionEnd, and the bodies of BOTH functions are byte-unchanged from main. Verify by extracting both function bodies from main and the branch and diffing them: only comment placement moves. CAM-389 is out of scope and extractCommandSubstitutionSpans must not be otherwise altered.
LIVE_DERIVATION_RE is byte-unchanged from main, since CAM-386 is out of scope. Verify by extracting the declaration from both main and the branch and diffing.

The frozen-comparand flagged-forms and passing-cases describe blocks gain at least one test per newly covered operator and at least one test for the mixed-clause case. The total test count in test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts strictly EXCEEDS main's count, with main's count derived live at check time via git show rather than frozen as a literal. No existing test is deleted or weakened.

MODULE PURITY PRESERVED, the hard contract this module declares at its header: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts still has exactly two import statements and introduces no fs, node:fs, Bun.file, Bun.spawn, Bun.$, Bun.write or child_process usage. The exported surface is unchanged: RuleFinding, OracleLintRule, PrdOracleLintFinding, RULES and lintPrd remain exported, lintStoryCriteria remains module-private, and the lintPrd signature is byte-identical to main's. The exported surface must additionally be oracled directly, not merely left to typecheck: diff the output of an '^export ' scan of the module against the same scan taken from main via git show, requiring an empty diff, and extract the lintPrd signature line from both and require it byte-identical.

Quality gates green: bun run typecheck zero errors, bun test with zero failures, bun run check:all passing. The total passing test count strictly exceeds main's baseline, derived live rather than compared against a frozen literal, and the failure count is zero.

Every story runs the full lint spine, not only the last one: `bun run check:all` is an oracle on EVERY story in this PRD, so a lint regression introduced by the first story fails that story rather than surfacing four stories later.
gotchas: HARD PROHIBITION, THIS IS WHY THE PREVIOUS PLAN ESCALATED: `bun test <file>` must NEVER be the sole gating oracle for a behavior criterion in this PRD. A story that ADDS tests can never make a test-file run red against main, because those tests do not exist on main, so such an oracle is structurally tautological and cannot distinguish a satisfying branch from main. The auditor measured `bun test ./test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts` green on main at 58 pass / 0 fail while it was attached to three criteria the issue had labelled red-on-main. Behavior criteria carry the verbatim behavioral oracle given in the criterion text; `bun test` may be an ADDITIONAL gate, never the criterion's oracle.

Every criterion in this spec that is behavior-bearing already carries its oracle VERBATIM, together with the red-or-green-on-main sweep result measured by the orchestrator at spec time against main @ 77481552. Use those commands as given. Do not paraphrase them, do not replace them with greps over test-file bytes, and annotate each criterion in the PRD with its sweep result. Grep oracles over a test file's bytes are satisfied by a comment or a test NAME without any test ever calling the rule.

prd-oracle-lint.ts is SIDECAR-EXECUTED at plan time: lintPrd is called from src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts via runOracleLintCheck, between the planner's prd.json presence guard and the auditor spawn. A rebuild plus sidecar respawn is therefore MANDATORY after merge, or the operator's own plan preflights keep running the old under-enforcing rule.

This module lints acceptance criteria. The criteria written FOR this story are themselves subject to the four rules it implements, including the very frozen-comparand rule being widened here, and the widening makes MORE operator shapes lintable than when these criteria were authored. Do not author a criterion comparing against a frozen literal count; derive every main-derived comparand at check time.

Prefer BEHAVIORAL oracles over grep oracles throughout: import RULES, find the rule by name, and call rule.test(command) directly. A grep for a regex source string is fragile and has repeatedly produced non-falsifiable oracles in this repo.

Every acceptance oracle must be swept RED against unmodified main before it is trusted, exhaustively rather than by sample. Two criteria here are deliberately GREEN pinning criteria and say so in their own text; they must not be reported as red.

ALWAYS print a row or case COUNT alongside any pass/fail sweep, so a zero-iteration sweep is visibly vacuous instead of silently green. This exact defect (a sweep that passed with zero iterations) is what the zero-match-vacuous rule exists to catch, and it has bitten this repo more than once.

NEVER hand-escape a multi-quote probe inline. Write it to a .ts file with a heredoc quoted as <<'EOF' and use String.raw for the case strings, then run it with bun. Shell-quoting errors bit three separate times during CAM-388, on a PR about shell quoting.

Neither src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts (633 lines) nor test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts (543 lines) appears in scripts/file-size-budget.json, verified against main @ 77481552, so there is no ceiling to raise for either. Do not add budget entries.

The test file's naming convention is 'flags X' for positive cases and 'does not flag X' for negative ones, with describe blocks named '<rule-name> rule: flagged forms' and '<rule-name> rule: passing cases', and the rule handle bound once per describe via findFrozenComparandRule(). Follow it for every added test; CAM-384 exists precisely because one test violated it.

ACCEPTED BLIND SPOT, recorded at scripts/cam/patterns.md:915 and NOT in scope to fix: frozen-comparand's quote-stripping unwraps `-c` interpreter payloads but NOT `-e` payloads, so a live comparison inside `bun -e '...'` is invisible to the rule. This is why the three rows of cam382-false-positives.txt all return false when passed to the rule as whole commands, and it is why their INNER cases, not the wrapper commands, are what belong in the matrix.

hasFrozenIntegerComparand currently emits at most one finding per command. Clause-level scoping makes multiple frozen comparands possible in one command; the OracleLintRule contract returns RuleFinding | null so it must still return a single finding, and the reason text must stay accurate when more than one clause is at fault.
domainTerms: frozen comparand: an acceptance-criterion oracle comparing against a literal integer captured once at authoring time, which rots silently when a later commit on main edits the compared file.
live derivation token: a `git show main:<path>`, `git diff main` or `git grep ... main` invocation that recomputes a comparand against main at check time instead of freezing it.
clause: a segment of a shell oracle command delimited by &&, ||, ; or newline, evaluated after quote-stripping; the unit at which the derivation excuse is scoped after this slice.

pinning criterion: an acceptance criterion deliberately green against main, present to prove an existing behavior did NOT change, as opposed to the normal red-against-main criterion proving new behavior was added.

fixture-shape guard: the assertions in the table-driven test that require the behavioral matrix to retain specific structural dimensions, so a future story cannot narrow the fixture back into vacuity without visibly failing.
